sources.headline: Oman rescues 25 from burning oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
sources.text: Incident comes as Iran says three oil tankers were halted while attempting to use ‘unauthorised routes’ to cross Hormuz.Oman has rescued 25 crew members from a burning crude oil tanker as ships continue to be targeted in the Strait of Hormuz.The Omani Maritime Security Centre said in a statement on Friday that it had evacuated the people aboard the RITI merchant ship. Oman said the vessel was flying the Panamanian flag, while the tracking website MarineTraffic identified it as a crude oil tanker.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Oil flows are up as Iran war turmoil eases. Why do prices keep rising?list 2 of 3Senators briefed on Trump’s ‘insane’ plan to restart war on Iranlist 3 of 3Qatari officials in Iran in bid to revive ceasefire deal with USend of listThe incident came as Iran said three oil tankers had been halted while attempting to use “unauthorised routes” to cross the Strait of Hormuz.It is unclear whether one of the vessels was the tanker whose crew were evacuated by Omani maritime authorities.Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said all three vessels were carrying oil and that one was a supertanker. It added that the ships had been halted following “incidents” or after hitting mines.“Two offending oil tankers, one in the eastern part and the other in the western part of the Strait of Hormuz, which were attempting to pass through the unauthorised route, encountered incidents and were brought to a halt in the waters south of the strait,” the IRGC said in a statement.Later, in a separate statement, the IRGC said a third tanker – a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of oil – “exploded and caught fire today as a result of attempting to pass through an unauthorised route”.Meanwhile, to the east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s navy said it struck and destroyed an unmanned enemy craft on Friday.Iran has repeatedly warned vessels against passing through the strait without Tehran’s permission.It has claimed responsibility for attacks on ships and said last month that vessels attempting to pass through the strait without authorisation would face “destruction”.Tehran has asserted control over much of the waterway since the US and Israel launched the war on February 28.The US military denies the naval mine claims. On Friday, United States Central Command chief Brad Cooper said the Strait of Hormuz’s “internationally recognised primary transit routes” had been successfully cleared of Iranian sea mines.

sources.headline: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard reports three tankers on fire in Strait of Hormuz as talks continue
sources.text:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday, Oct. 30, that three oil tankers had encountered incidents while attempting to navigate routes Tehran considers unauthorized in the eastern and western sections of the Strait of Hormuz. All vessels were subsequently stopped in the waterway’s southern waters.
According to Iranian state media, the Guard claimed the tankers had switched off their navigation and positioning systems and were attempting to leave the strait through routes opposed by Tehran, with the support of the U.S. military.
The Guard said the vessels continued sailing despite repeated radio warnings before encountering trouble in what it described as unsafe areas.
It provided no details about the tankers’ identities, their flags, the precise cause of the incidents or the condition of their crews.
The reports came as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday to continue efforts to broker an agreement between Iran and the United States.
Uncertainty over the number of tankers damaged
In a separate incident whose possible connection to the Guard’s claims remains unclear, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, or UKMTO, reported that a small boat approached an oil tanker Thursday evening and attached two explosive devices to its hull above the waterline.
The devices detonated, sparking a fire in the engine room and temporarily disabling the vessel.
The Financial Times identified the tanker as the Louise 1.
The incident occurred about 25 nautical miles (46 kilometers) northeast of Khasab, Oman.
UKMTO said the fire had been extinguished, all crew members were safe and no environmental pollution had been reported. The tanker subsequently resumed its voyage toward its next port.
The attack appeared to mark the first reported successful use of limpet mines against a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz since the U.S.-Iran war began in February 2026.
It was not immediately clear who was responsible or whether the attack was connected to the Guard’s latest claims involving two tankers.
Separately, Oman’s Maritime Security Center reported Friday that the Royal Navy of Oman had evacuated 25 crew members from a Panama-flagged commercial vessel that came under attack and caught fire about 1.6 nautical miles off the coast of Musandam.
The center said the crew members received necessary medical care but did not identify the vessel or those responsible for the attack.
It remained unclear whether the incident was connected to other reported attacks on tankers in the strait.
The Guard’s latest statements followed claims Thursday, Oct. 29, that three tankers had struck naval mines along the strait’s southern route, triggering explosions and fires.
Iran’s regular military also reported Thursday that another tanker had caught fire in the eastern Strait of Hormuz.
According to Agence France-Presse, Iranian officials claimed that all four vessels had been operating in prohibited and unsafe areas.
However, it remained unclear whether the two tankers mentioned in Friday’s Guard statement were additional vessels or were among those involved in the incidents reported Thursday.
U.S. Central Command disputes Iranian claims
Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz’s main shipping lanes had been cleared of Iranian naval mines.
He also claimed that Iran’s navy had been destroyed and that Revolutionary Guard forces were no longer operating in the waterway.
Cooper said U.S. forces remained in the region to keep major shipping routes open and secure.
CENTCOM also rejected a claim made Thursday by the Revolutionary Guard that it had taken control of an American MQM-170 Outlaw drone in the western Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian sources, meanwhile, reported Friday that an American unmanned surface vessel had been destroyed in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military had neither confirmed nor denied that report at the time of publication.
The growing number of maritime incidents comes amid a continuing dispute between Washington and Tehran over the routes used by commercial shipping through the strategic waterway.
Iran has demanded that vessels coordinate their movements with Iranian authorities and use routes closer to the strait’s northern shores. Ships seeking to avoid Iranian control have instead used the southern route.
Qatari mediators return to Tehran amid threats of renewed U.S. strikes
Diplomatic efforts to prevent another major escalation in the U.S.-Iran war are continuing alongside mounting military tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.
CBS News, citing a source familiar with the negotiations, reported signs of progress and said Iran was expected to respond to a revised proposal from Qatari mediators by the end of the week.
The diplomatic initiative is aimed at preventing a resumption of large-scale U.S. strikes against Iran, a possibility President Donald Trump has repeatedly raised in recent weeks.
Axios reported that Qatari-led mediators were seeking common ground on issues including inspections of Iran’s nuclear facilities and sanctions relief.
However, disagreements persisted over the conditions for formally opening negotiations.
Axios also reported that the United States and Israel were considering options for extensive military strikes against Iran after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections.
The Associated Press reported Thursday, citing two diplomats, that Washington had warned several regional allies about the possibility of renewed U.S. attacks on Iran and potential Iranian retaliation, although Trump had not made a final decision.
Trump, speaking Friday to a Kansas City radio station, said the war with Iran would end "soon," but did not specify whether that would be achieved through a diplomatic agreement or military action.
The U.S. president reiterated that Washington wanted guarantees that Iran would never acquire a nuclear weapon.
His remarks came as there was still no clear indication that Tehran and Washington had reached an agreement on the conditions for ending the war, while the possibility of renewed large-scale military strikes remained on the table.

2:39 AM
U.S. military death toll since start of Iran war rises to 23, Pentagon says
The U.S. Department of Defense has added two more service member deaths to its official account of casualties since the war with Iran started more than eight months ago, bringing the overall death toll to 23. Both of the newly noted deaths on the Defense Casualty Analysis System portal were noncombat related. In total the DCAS portal says 11 service members have been killed by enemy fire during the war, and 12 others have died under circumstances deemed nonhostile, which includes accidents and sickness.Both of the service members recently added as nonhostile deaths were airmen, including one who died of an illness and the another from unspecified causes that remain under investigation, The Washington Post quoted the Air Force as saying.The two deaths added to the DCAS system are listed under Overseas Operations, which includes deaths recorded by the Pentagon after it stopped using the name Operation Epic Fury for the offensive against Iran in May, after Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared the operation over.
1:42 AM
Saudi coalition says it intercepted Houthi drone in Mecca region
The Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Mecca region that had been fired by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels."A drone launched by the terrorist Houthi militia has been intercepted and destroyed in the Mecca region," the coalition wrote in a post on X.The Houthis denied any attempt to strike Saudi Arabia on Friday, the Reuters news agency reports.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on social media that the group hadn't conducted any operations aimed at Saudi territory, adding that the Houthis only target Saudi oil facilities and military bases.CBS/AFP
5:11 PM / October 29, 2026
Blasts heard in Riyadh as Saudis down 2 ballistic missiles, officials say
Explosions rocked the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh on Thursday hours after the Iran-backed Houthis reported deadly strikes earlier in the day on residential areas of western Yemen that the Houthis said killed at least 12 people.The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said on Thursday it had downed two ballistic missiles launched by the group towards Riyadh, soon after Agence France-Presse correspondents heard fresh explosions in the capital. "Air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said on X. Earlier, AFP correspondents in Riyadh had heard at least eight explosions as authorities warned the city was "under a hostile aerial threat" in a phone alert.Saudi civil defense had issued warnings for "potential danger" in Riyadh, Kharj and the southern city of Najran that were lifted shortly afterward. The Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on the Riyadh airport that forced its shuttering for two weeks as flagship events were canceled, threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.The Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Yemeni government have exchanged daily attacks since a yearslong truce fell apart over the summer.
2:37 PM / October 29, 2026
Tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz, U.K. navy says
A tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz around 7:30 p.m. local time (noon Eastern time), according to the U.K. Marine Trade Operations Centre.The ship was exiting the strait along the southern route, promoted by the U.S., when it came under fire. "There are no reported injuries to the crew or environmental impact … at this time," the UKMTO said. While it wasn't clear who fired the projectile, Iran has taken credit for several ships hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday and has been targeting ships along the southern route at an increased rate.
12:57 PM / October 29, 2026
Iran has not yet responded to letter from Vance, Iranian media says
Iran has not yet responded to a letter sent by Vice President JD Vance to the secretary of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, according to the semi-official Tasnim News agency, which is closely affiliated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.Tasnim said in a Thursday post on its official Telegram social media account that Tehran was not prepared to drop any of its core conditions for a ceasefire, which include lifting the American blockade of Iran's ports, easing sanctions and giving Iran access to its frozen financial assets held abroad, among other things.Multiple news outlets have reported that Vance's letter to Rezaei was an attempt to restart peace negotiations, but President Trump said Wednesday that it was a focused outreach intended only to help get medical supplies into Iran.
12:22 PM / October 29, 2026
Iranian navy says another oil tanker has been struck by a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz
Iran's navy said a tanker it described as violating maritime restrictions was damaged and caught fire after striking sea mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the vessel unable to continue sailing.In a statement, the navy said the incident occurred before noon on Thursday as the tanker was sailing through an area designated as prohibited and unsafe by IranThe U.S. has encouraged shippers to use a shipping route in the south of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has insisted vessels can only use northern routes it has authorized.The navy's statement warned that the Strait of Hormuz was closed "to violating vessels that, without coordination and relying on the lies of the U.S. president, intend to pass through prohibited and unsafe areas.""These uncoordinated transits through high-risk areas have exposed and will continue to expose vessels and their crews to serious dangers," it added.
11:38 AM / October 29, 2026
Qatar denies interfering in Israeli elections, accuses politicians of disinformation campaign
Qatar has categorically denied allegations of interfering in Israel's elections or funding efforts to influence their outcome, accusing Israeli politicians and media figures of launching a disinformation campaign to drag the small Persian Gulf state into domestic Israeli political disputes.Foreign Ministry spokesman Majid al-Ansari said in a statement that Qatar would not be used as a scapegoat for Israeli politicians' failures, insisting that Doha had no involvement in Israel's political competition and would continue its mediation efforts between Iran and the U.S., as well as wider diplomatic engagement and support for the Palestinian people.His comments come after Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that Tuesday's national elections were "stolen by Arab parties" and claimed foreign interference in the vote.Israel's Shin Bet internal security service is investigating possible Qatari and Turkish funding used in an effort to influence the election outcome, according to reports by the Jerusalem Post and Israel's Channel 13."These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure," al-Ansari said. "The repeated invocation of Qatar in Israeli electoral rhetoric reveals an excessive obsession with our country among certain Israeli political and media figures."
11:10 AM / October 29, 2026
Iran's navy claims 20 successful attacks on U.S. warships, 300 attacks on U.S. interests
Iran's navy has carried out more than 20 operations against U.S. warships and approximately 300 operations targeting American interests in various locations during the war, Iranian Army Navy Coordinating Deputy Rear Admiral Jalil Moghadam said in an interview published Thursday by the official state-run news agency IRNA.Moghadam claimed the operations involved missiles and drones and said Iran's navy remains operational despite repeated claims by President Trump and other U.S. officials saying it has been destroyed."If the Iranian Navy has been destroyed, why have these forces not come closer than 500 or 600 kilometers to the Strait of Hormuz, or closer than 300 kilometers to our maritime borders? There is a force standing in their way, and that force must be the Navy," he said.Moghadam did not offer any evidence to substantiate his claims.
10:27 AM / October 29, 2026
Iran's IRGC challenges U.S. to "prove your claim of mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz"
IRGC spokesperson Brig. Gen. Abolfazl Mohebi challenged U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) to provide independent evidence for its claims of mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz."Prove your claim of mine-clearing in the Strait of Hormuz with independent evidence, not a statement!" demanded Mohebi in a post on X, adding that "the reality of the Strait of Hormuz is determined in the skies, on land and at sea — not on social media or in America's media-warfare rooms."Earlier Thursday the IRGC said three oil tankers had been disabled after striking mines in the strait, and the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center confirmed one vess

sources.headline: Ship reported on fire off Oman as Iran escalation fears mount
sources.text:
A ship on fire has been reported in the Strait of Hormuz, British maritime agency UKMTO said on Thursday.
The agency, which is run by the British Royal Navy, did not give details on the cause of the blaze or any casualties.
Iran has, however, recently stepped up its attacks on ships that it sees as using the waterway without proper authorization.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said in a statement on Thursday that three tankers had exploded and caught fire in the past 24 hours after hitting sea mines while using an "unauthorized" route, but it is not known if the case reported to the UKMTO is one of them.
This comes as Iran has reported shooting down another US drone east of the waterway as fears grow of a new escalation in the US-Iran war. Iran steps up attacks in Strait of Hormuz
The UKMTO said the captain of another ship had reported the blaze onboard a vessel spotted 9 nautical miles (17 kilometers) north of the town of Khasab in Oman, which is located just off the strait.
The status of ⁠the ​crew is ​unknown, and so far ​no information has emerged pertaining to ⁠damage or environmental ⁠impact.
Since the Middle East war was triggered in February by US and Israeli attacks on Iran, Tehran has sought to control the strait, a key transit point for global oil and natural gas supplies, and has attacked ships it considers to be unauthorized users of the waterway.
Oil exports through the waterway fell again last week, according to shipping data provider Kpler.
Attacks on ships in the strait are at the highest level since the war began, according to US-based think tank Washington Institute for Near East Policy.
The US Navy, which is enforcing its own blockade of Iranian vessels, has recently escorted tankers through the strait in the area where the burning ship was reportedly sighted.The Strait of Hormuz is a vital chokepoint for oil and gas transportImage: REUTERS
US drone downed
The reported ship fire comes as Iran says its forces have downed a drone near the strait, with the Tasnim news agency citing the IRGC as saying a new, advanced air defense system was used.
The report said that Iran's armed forces have destroyed 14 drones of this type and more than 50 MQ-9 Reaper drones since the war broke out.
The claims have not been independently verified, though the US Congressional Research Service says dozens of US aircraft and drones have been reported lost or damaged since the war began.The MQ-1 Predator can be used both for surveillance and attackImage: Col. Leslie Pratt/epa/picture alliance
Fears of new US strikes
The latest incidents come as US President Donald Trump is widely seen to be considering fresh strikes against Iran after the US midterm elections on November 3.
Last week, Trump said, "we may do another little Epic Fury," referring to the US-Israeli attacks on Tehran in February that triggered the war. He did not, however, give any timeframe.
A third US aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are currently heading to the region.
As reports of a possible renewed escalation swirl, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has reportedly nonetheless fired the Pentagon's top military planner, Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia.
If confirmed, the ouster would be the latest in a series of such high-level departures under the Trump administration, with Sylvia's predecessor, Lieutenant General Joseph McGee being forced to retire last October.
According to a report in The Atlantic, no reason was given for Sylvia's departure and no replacement has been named.Iran conflict: Could a new phase of the war be imminent?To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
